result.summary: Adds the `p2p_1p1c_liveness` fuzz target to exercise opportunistic one-parent-one-child (1p1c) package relay end-to-end. The target initializes a full PeerManager, validation engine, and active chainstate against fuzzer-controlled peers to assert that an honest peer announcing an acceptable package child eventually gets it accepted into the mempool regardless of adversarial peers stalling, disconnecting, malleating transactions, or delivering witness-stripped variants.
result.problem: Existing transaction download manager fuzz targets mock and model validation results rather than running real validation logic. Consequently, they cannot verify how actual validation return states (such as reconsiderable fee failures, missing inputs, and witness malleations) interact with cross-peer download accounting and reject filters to prevent transaction censorship.
evidence: PR description: 'The existing download-manager targets model validation results, so they cannot check how real results are attributed across peers.'

Commit 3b16af7e7a notes that without targeted testing and invariants, bugs where a malleated parent from one peer cancels orphan resolution for another peer can easily survive tens of thousands of fuzz iterations ('reverting the witnessless-parent fix survived 57k runs').
result.scope_notes: This PR is stacked on top of open PR #36369. Nine of the ten commits and all consensus/P2P/validation diffs belong to #36369; only the final commit adding `src/test/fuzz/p2p_1p1c_liveness.cpp` (+402 lines) is unique to this pull request.
result.changed_since_previous: Diff is now available; the PR remains stacked on #36369 with no changes to the proposed fuzzing harness approach.
result.card: Adds the p2p_1p1c_liveness fuzz target to test end-to-end 1p1c package relay liveness using live PeerManager, P2P message processing, and validation components. Existing download manager harnesses model validation results rather than invoking validation directly, leaving blind spots where adversarial peers delivering malleated transactions or triggering specific validation failures could disrupt package resolution from honest peers. The harness asserts that acceptable packages announced by honest peers always enter the mempool despite adversary stalls, malleation, or disconnections. Stacked on #36369, which provides the underlying fixes and base test updates.

risk.why: The PR's unique contribution is exclusively a new fuzzing harness target; bugs would only affect local fuzz test executions.
